findings.claim: With the tier optional, deleting a declared tier strict while other hooks keys remain no longer steps the hooks down on a bare or forced re-render (base: strict to standard by the accidental pin; fold: strict stays), while the schema and wiki text 're-run totem hook install --force after changing it' implied the deletion would; consistent with the mmnto-ai/totem#2753 survive rule and failing toward strict, but a direction change the changeset and the Amendment did not disclose.
findings.counterexample: Measured on both revisions in a scratch repository: hooks with tier strict and legsOwed installed, the tier line deleted, --force re-render: base standard, fold strict (and with the whole block deleted both revisions keep strict). FOLDED as disclosure (1e58a2c6), ranked MINOR by the seat since the direction is the ruled one: the schema comment, config-reference.md, hook-integration.md, the changeset and the Amendment say stepping down is a declaration (tier standard, or --standard) and that deleting the line keeps the installed tier.

findings.claim: doctor --parity renders its git-hook canonical at the configured tier (standard when none is declared), so a --strict-installed hook under a tier-less hooks block reads as drift whose --force remedy no longer clears it; the loop existed at the base for a config with no hooks block and the fold extends it to every tier-less block.
findings.counterexample: hooks with legsOwed only and a --strict install: parity warns, --force keeps strict, parity warns again. FOLDED as remedy text (1e58a2c6, then the copy-paste-safe form): the remediation says to declare hooks.tier or pass --standard; aligning parity's tier axis with the Git Hooks row's installed-tier read (A10) is named a follow-up in the changeset, the wiki and the Amendment, not changed here.

findings.claim: The installer test covered less than the prose: bare path only (no --force, no init path, no hook-manager path), pre-push only in two segments, and no shield-only shape at the schema, resolver or installer; the root cause is pinned at the resolver every path reads, and the leg's probe confirmed all six paths.
findings.counterexample: FOLDED (1e58a2c6): the schema test takes shield-only and a legsOwed-plus-shield block, the resolver test takes shield-only, the installer test re-renders with --force and reads both hooks in every segment; the init and hook-manager paths stay measured by the leg's grid and are disclosed as such.

findings.claim: Two questions for the seat: the branch carried a deposit commit above the read's head that the read did not cover; and the base column of the grid came from the main checkout's built dist rather than a build of the base commit made by the leg.

verdict: Second read, re-armed on the tier-resolution fold and scoped to it (the two commits ending at this head), by one falsification leg: blocking=0 material=1 minor=3 question=1, counts as typed; folded=5. The leg measured the full differential grid through the built dist of both revisions (seven config shapes x three installed tiers x six installer paths) and found exactly the four rows the fold intended changed, every other cell identical, the three readers of the parsed tier unchanged and defensive, the exported type loosened only, the Git Hooks compare unchanged, and the init refactor byte-identical in prompt and disclosure strings to the inline block it replaced.
